memoryTip: Im-placable: can’t be placated — won’t be soothed.
correctPassage: An implacable foe of the treaty refused every compromise.
wrongPassages: The station’s implacable gate display counted down to a train that never came.
The sérac traverse felt implacable on a marked winter route with wands.
Fans called the deluxe remaster implacable for loudness that crushed dynamics.

definition: tending to obstruct or harm; unfriendly
memoryTip: Enemy-ical — harmful or unfriendly.
correctPassage: Conditions on the planet’s surface are inimical to known forms of life.
wrongPassages: The subtonic drone was inimical under a Picardy third that ignored it.
He treated the formality as inimical and skipped it without consequence.
The plaza design was inimical: benches faced away from one another.

definition: attribute something, often a fault, to someone
memoryTip: Im-pute: put the blame (or quality) on someone.
correctPassage: It is unfair to impute bad motives without evidence.
wrongPassages: The terminal’s impute art wall was a vinyl wrap of a different airport.

an impute border crossing still requires passports, checks, and stamps.

definition: tending to keep a firm hold; persistent
memoryTip: Tenax = holding tight — won’t let go.
correctPassage: Tenacious reporting eventually uncovered the source of the leak.
wrongPassages: The bog hollow stayed tenacious after every free-running ditch lowered it.
His tenacious limitation clause ran longer than the rest of the agreement.
Her tenacious testimony contradicted itself on both times and names.

memoryTip: Salute to health — beneficial effect (even if harsh).
correctPassage: The failure had a salutary effect: teams began documenting assumptions.
wrongPassages: Her salutary printer note described a binding style never used in production.
Fans called the live-stream mix salutary for chat audio over the performance.

memoryTip: Delusion-ive — creates a false belief.
correctPassage: The hope of a quick fix proved delusive.
wrongPassages: The epilogue was delusive: it opened a sequel instead of closing the story.

The snow cornice felt delusive behind a seasonal fence and signs.

memoryTip: Tortured path — full of twists (or overly long argument).
correctPassage: A tortuous legal path delayed the project for years.
wrongPassages: Historians labeled the decade tortuous once complete archives left almost nothing in doubt.
Trustees cut the tortuous arts grant that local schools had already matched.
The team hoped to tortuous reopen rates by locking closed tickets permanently.

memoryTip: Fur-tive like a thief’s fur sneak — secretive glance.
correctPassage: He cast a furtive glance at the clock during the interview.
wrongPassages: The bog hollow stayed furtive after drains lowered the entire water table.

She practiced the speech furtive until every pause landed the same way.

memoryTip: De-bunk: knock the bunk (nonsense) out — expose as false.
correctPassage: The article seeks to debunk popular myths about memory.
wrongPassages: The alliance was debunk: both sides published the full text of every clause.

a debunk game day is a pizza lunch with the runbook left closed.

memoryTip: Gold hallmark stamp — distinctive sign of quality.
correctPassage: Clarity is the hallmark of her scientific writing.
wrongPassages: The station’s hallmark wayfinding pointed every arrow toward “more soon.”

memoryTip: Can inter-change — swap without difference.
correctPassage: In this model the two variables are not interchangeable.
wrongPassages: The tidal pool stayed interchangeable behind a flap gate welded shut.
Critics called the ending interchangeable because it answered every question in the first act.

memoryTip: In a capsule — sum up the essence briefly.
correctPassage: One sentence can rarely encapsulate a decade of research.
wrongPassages: She tried to encapsulate the rumor mill by posting an unconfirmed theory online.

definition: treating serious issues with deliberate humor
memoryTip: Facet + joking face — treating serious things lightly on purpose.
correctPassage: A facetious remark during the briefing was widely misread as policy.
wrongPassages: She kept a facetious schedule: the same three tasks at the same times each day.

definition: not seen or visited by many people; private
memoryTip: Se-clude: shut away — private, hard to reach.
correctPassage: The cabin sits in a secluded valley far from any road.
wrongPassages: The tonic held was secluded under a coda that ended on V instead.
The bog pool stayed secluded when forestry drains crossed the moss.
The tenor pedal was secluded after the bass moved on without it.

memoryTip: Re-trieve: bring back (like a retriever dog).
correctPassage: Software can retrieve deleted files for a limited time.
wrongPassages: She marked the go-live retrieve while data migration was still running.

definition: make look or feel younger or more vital
memoryTip: Re-juvenile: make young/fresh again.
correctPassage: A new arts festival helped rejuvenate the downtown district.
wrongPassages: They hoped to rejuvenate the protest by filming empty chairs as a show of unity.

memoryTip: Abstract + obtuse difficulty — hard to understand.
correctPassage: The proof is abstruse even for specialists in the field.
wrongPassages: Committees shelved the abstruse pilot that users had rated highest.

definition: demonstrating aggression and willingness to fight
memoryTip: Belli = war — eager to fight.
correctPassage: Bellicose rhetoric made a diplomatic solution harder to reach.
wrongPassages: The wetlands stayed bellicose behind pumps that held water at one fixed level.

Fans found the spatial remix bellicose for dialogue lost outside the screen.

memoryTip: Caco (bad) + phony (sound) — harsh noise mix.
correctPassage: A cacophony of car horns filled the street at rush hour.
wrongPassages: Voters blocked the cacophony park bond that trail groups had backed.

memoryTip: Delete-erious: deletes health — harmful.
correctPassage: Even low levels of the chemical may have deleterious effects.
wrongPassages: Her deleterious temporary restraining order draft lacked a proposed bond amount.
